info.title: Oila 360 API
info.description: Main backend API (https://api.oila360.uz/docs/api.json), merged with the high-frequency device-telemetry ingest service (https://api.oila360.uz/docs/ingestion.json). Captured live 2026-08-13. Both documents sit behind HTTP basic auth; /api/docs-json — the URL this snapshot used to be fetched from, and which OpenAPI/README.md records as 404 — was replaced by those two paths, so this file IS refreshable again.

mode.description: audio = mic only, video = camera + mic

delivered.description: Whether FCM accepted the push. FALSE is a soft failure: stream.* has no poll fallback, so the device will never hear the command — fail fast, do not wait. TRUE does NOT mean the child is publishing yet.

transport.description: Informational only. 'poll' is a lie for stream.* (there is no stream-command poll endpoint) — it is reused because DispatchResult allows only these three. Switch on `delivered` alone.

room.description: Server-derived LiveKit room. Join this — never re-derive it client-side.

maxDurationSeconds.description: Server-owned lease. The child stops publishing when it expires; re-POST /stream/start at roughly half this to renew while the live screen is open.

delivered.description: Whether FCM accepted the push. FALSE is a soft failure: stream.* has no poll fallback, so the device will never hear the command — fail fast, do not wait. TRUE does NOT mean the child is publishing yet.

transport.description: Informational only. 'poll' is a lie for stream.* (there is no stream-command poll endpoint) — it is reused because DispatchResult allows only these three. Switch on `delivered` alone.

room.description: Server-derived LiveKit room. Join this — never re-derive it client-side.

lastMessageId.description: Read up to and including this message id

ts.description: Device-side capture time. MUST be a UTC ISO-8601 instant ending in `Z` — a zoneless string is rejected. Past timestamps are kept as-is (an offline backlog is normal); a timestamp more than 60s in the future is clamped to server time and excluded from geofencing, which means a wrong handset clock silently loses crossings.

battery.description: Charge percentage, 0–100. Crossing the low threshold alerts the parent once.

diagnostics.description: Why this handset can or cannot do what the parent expects (D-102): granted permissions, special access, and device-wide settings that are not permissions at all (the GPS master switch, iOS Background App Refresh). Known keys: location, locationBackground, locationServices, batteryOptimization, backgroundRefresh, usageAccess, accessibility, overlay, notifications, microphone, camera, autoStart, lowPowerMode. Send only the keys this platform and build actually measure — an omitted key means "never reported" and is merged over the stored value, never treated as denied. An unknown key rejects the whole request, so the server always ships before a build that adds one.

name.description: User-visible label, for the parent’s list.

items.description: The FULL current installed set. Anything previously installed and missing here is flagged uninstalled, so a partial payload silently removes the rest.

usedSeconds.description: Seconds used SINCE THE LAST REPORT, not the running total — the server adds this to the device-local day. Sending a total re-adds it every cycle.

packageName.description: The app the removal was attempted on — usually this app itself.

applicationName.description: User-visible label; goes straight into the parent’s notification copy.

child.description: The child's CURRENT identity. A parent may rename the child or change the emoji, colour or photo at any time, so this is the only correct source — the copy in the `POST /api/v1/device/pair` response is a snapshot of pairing day.

screenTime.description: Identical to the body of `GET /api/v1/device/apps/screen-time`. Everything is SECONDS. Null limits mean the parent has set no budget — a normal state, not a missing value.

recent.description: At most two rows, for a preview. This is NOT a substitute for `GET /api/v1/device/tasks`: it carries no pagination and no status filter, so a caller that needs a particular selection (pending vs. completed vs. cancelled) must still walk that route.

lastMessage.description: Null on a thread with no messages yet.

AttributionTouchDto.description: Transcribed 2026-08-18 from the server's own ValidationPipe rather than from the published spec, which sits behind basic auth: an empty POST names the required fields and their enums, and `forbidNonWhitelisted` names every declared optional one by refusing everything else with 'property X should not exist'. So the property SET is exact; the string constraints (length, pattern) are not — the pipe does not report those for a value it never reaches.

storeReviewMode.description: True only when this exact platform/build pair is the one an operator recorded as under store review, the master toggle is on, and any configured expiry is still in the future. Treat any error or timeout as FALSE.

SelfUnpairDto.description: Field list derived from the published route documentation itself, not from the component schema (the document was received truncated before `components`). The 403 text states `pin` is optional and that the call succeeds with no `pin` at all when none is set. String constraints (length, pattern) were NOT captured and are deliberately omitted rather than guessed.

SetUnpairPinDto.description: Field list derived from the published route documentation itself, not from the component schema (the document was received truncated before `components`). The route exists to set a PIN, so `pin` is required. String constraints (length, pattern) were NOT captured and are deliberately omitted rather than guessed.

accepted.description: Rows written. Always equals `items.length` on success — a future-dated fix is NOT rejected, it is clamped to server time and still counted here (it is only excluded from geofencing). So this is a write receipt, not a validation result: do not diff it against what you sent to decide whether to resend.

updated.description: Always `true` — the snapshot is persisted. Carries no state back: the battery-low alert and the parent-facing `device:status` frame are server-side side-effects the child never sees.

synced.description: Packages upserted. Counts DISTINCT package names, so a payload that repeats one reports it once — this can be lower than `items.length` without anything failing.

removed.description: Packages that were installed and are absent from this payload; flagged uninstalled, NOT deleted, so the parent’s lock/limit survives a reinstall (D-037). Send the FULL installed set every time — a partial sync marks everything you omitted as removed.

usageDate.description: Today by the DEVICE-LOCAL calendar (`Device.timezone`, captured at pairing) — not the server day. Limits reset at the child’s midnight.

usedSeconds.description: What the server holds for this package on `usageDate`, after this report.

dailyLimitSeconds.description: Parent-set daily limit. `null` = no limit configured for this app.

remainingSeconds.description: Floored at 0. `null` when `dailyLimitSeconds` is null, never a misleading 0.

isLimitReached.description: True once `usedSeconds >= dailyLimitSeconds`. Always false when there is no limit.

lockedPackages.description: The FULL effectively-blocked set for this device right now — parent-locked apps plus apps over today’s limit. Enforce exactly this list and drop whatever you were enforcing before; it is not a delta, and it covers apps absent from your payload.

stats.description: One line per DISTINCT package in your payload — nothing else. It is the reply to what you just reported, not the device’s whole day; use `GET /device/apps/screen-time` for the device-wide total.

usedSeconds.description: Seconds this app was on screen on `date`, counted from that day’s local midnight — the day’s figure so far, NOT the seconds since your last report. It replaces what the server holds for this app on that day.

date.description: The handset’s local calendar day, YYYY-MM-DD. A day outside [today − 7, today + 1] (today by the child profile’s timezone) is skipped, not rejected.

items.description: Every app with screen time on `date`; a package appears at most once. An app left out reads 0 for that day, and `[]` says the day had no screen time at all.

days.description: One entry per local day, each date at most once. Today plus up to 7 days back.

lockedPackages.description: The FULL effectively-blocked set for this device right now — parent-locked apps plus apps over today’s limit, judged on today’s figures after this report was written. Enforce exactly this list and drop whatever you were enforcing before.

stats.description: One line per package in TODAY’s entry of your report, and nothing else. Empty when the report has no entry for today (by `Device.timezone`) — earlier days get no lines.

usedSeconds.description: Device-wide total across every app for `date`. Server-summed from the same rows the parent’s summary reads, so the two surfaces cannot disagree — do not recompute it from `UsageStatsManager` locally.

dailyScreenLimitSeconds.description: The parent’s daily budget, DISPLAY-ONLY — nothing enforces it. `null` = no budget set.

remainingSeconds.description: Floored at 0. `null` when no budget is set — render “no limit”, not “0 left”.

reported.description: Always `true` — the report was accepted. It does NOT mean the parent has been notified: the alert rides a durable queue and the feed row + push are written by the other service moments later.
